text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Presidential elections are scheduled for June 15 and should be officially announced in a week, government sources say.
- Textile company Varteks will sign a new five-year licence contract with denim maker Levi Strauss & Co in May on condition that Varteks is fully privatised in 18 months.

- Foreign investment fund managers led by Raiffeisen Zentral Bank visit state privatisation agency to enquire about companies including electrical concern Koncar and Adriatic Pipeline, which will be floated later this year.
- Dukat dairy to import 10,000 heifers to boost production, says general manager for milk purchase Mirko Brcic.
- Minister of Economy Nenad Porges meets with U.S. trade ministry officials Stuart Eitenstat and Franklin Varga. The two countries should soon endorse an agreement on the protection of investments.
- Parking payment to be made easier when magnetic cards are introduced in June says director of Zagreb Parking Mate Kraljevic.
- Head of the supreme court Milan Vukovic warns candidates for future presidential elections against promising changes in the Croatian court system as a 'trump card' in their campaigns.
- Regent Pacific plans to open closed-end investment fund and invest up to $15 million in Croatian blue chips in the next three years, top manager James Mellon says. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
